transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um, I'm here because for the past year, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. It's really wearing me down. 

No matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I actually saw. I look at these things all day for work, so I know what I'm looking at, and I know they're altering his file. It's just exhausting trying to get anyone to listen to me.
Aside from your dad’s lab results, have you had any other beliefs that other people say are untrue?

No. Um... no, nothing else. It's really just this situation with his chart. I don't have any other... things that people tell me aren't true. Everything else in my life is just normal day-to-day stuff. It's strictly just his lab results.
Have you ever found any actual proof that the lab results were changed?

Well, that's the thing. I don't have, like, a smoking gun piece of paper yet. But I don't need one to know what I saw. I'm a phlebotomist, I look at these kinds of printouts every single day. I know what a normal CBC and metabolic panel look like, and I know what I saw on the screen when they first pulled it up compared to the printout they handed me later. 

Like I said before, I've spent the last year trying to prove that someone in the system is altering or hiding parts of his results. My family and the doctors keep saying the numbers are fine, but I know the chart they have now doesn't match the original. I just... I haven't been able to get my hands on the original file to prove it yet, and it's just really wearing me down.
If we were able to show you the original lab file and it matched the current numbers exactly, would you be able to accept that no one changed it?

I... no, I wouldn't. Because if you showed me a file that matched the current numbers, it would just mean you're showing me the fake file. 

Like I said, I've been dealing with this for a whole year. I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his lab results. And it doesn't matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. I know it. So if you showed me a paper that matched the fake numbers, it just means the original is still being hidden. It's just... it's really wearing me down trying to get someone to understand this.
Do you think the people changing the lab results are specifically targeting you, or is this just about your dad’s chart?

I don't think it has anything to do with me, honestly. I'm just... I don't know why anyone would target me specifically. I'm not anyone important. 

It's just about his chart. I don't know what their motives are or why they felt the need to alter his specific results, I just know that they did. So, no, I don't think they're after me or anything like that. It's strictly about whatever they're trying to hide in my dad's bloodwork.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t notice?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I'm not hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there. I'm completely sane, doctor. I just know what I saw on that computer screen regarding my dad's labs, and it doesn't match the paperwork they keep trying to hand me. But no, no hallucinations or anything like that.
Has this belief been affecting your work, relationships, or daily life?

Yes, it has. I mean, it's definitely caused some friction. My family... they've actually started leaving me out of the planning for my dad's appointments. They just do it without me now, I guess because they don't want me bringing up the lab results again. 

And at work, it's... well, I'm a phlebotomist, so I work in a lab setting myself. I feel like I'm being passed over for supervision roles now. It seems like people think I make issues with records too confrontational. But I'm just trying to make sure things are accurate, you know? But yeah, it's definitely affecting things.
Have you had any periods of feeling unusually depressed or unusually energized that lasted for days or longer around the same time as this belief?

No, I haven't. I mean, I get frustrated about the whole situation with my dad's chart, obviously, but... no, I haven't been depressed. And I definitely haven't had any weird energy spikes or anything like that. My mood is just... normal. I'm just a normal person trying to figure out why they changed his records.
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other recreational drugs around the time this belief started?

No, I don't use any of that. I don't drink, I don't smoke weed, and I definitely don't use any kind of recreational drugs or stimulants. I need to have a clear head for my job, and... well, I just don't do those things anyway. So no, nothing like that.
Have you ever had trouble telling what was real in any other way, like becoming confused about whether other things people said or did were real?

No, never. I've never had any trouble like that. I know exactly what's real and what isn't. The only thing I'm confused about is why they felt the need to alter my dad's medical records. But as far as, like, being confused about reality or what people are doing... no, nothing like that at all.
Have you ever had any depressive or manic episode before this belief started?

No, I haven't. Like I said, my mood has always been pretty normal. I've never had anything like a... a depressive episode or a manic episode, not before all this started with my dad's chart, and not after. I'm just a regular person.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that others would say are bizarre or clearly untrue, even if they were not about your dad’s lab results?

No, I haven't. I don't have any strange beliefs or... or anything like that. Everything else in my life is completely normal. I'm just focused on my work and trying to get to the bottom of why those numbers were changed. That's it.
Has this belief ever spread to other things, like believing the clinic is also tampering with other records or that someone is spying on you?

No, no, nothing like that. I don't think they're messing with anyone else's files, and I definitely don't think anyone is spying on me or following me around or anything. It's just my dad's chart. That's the only thing they altered.
Has this belief been going on continuously for at least six months?
Yeah, longer than six months. It's been going on for about a year now. Basically ever since my father's medical problems started requiring frequent labs and appointments. That's when it all started.
Have you ever had trouble organizing your thoughts so that other people said your speech was hard to follow or didn’t make sense?

No, not at all. People understand me perfectly fine. I don't have any trouble... organizing my thoughts or speaking. I mean, I communicate clearly every day at work. Being a phlebotomist, I have to be really precise when I'm talking to patients and the rest of the staff. My thoughts make complete sense.
Before this started about a year ago, had you ever had a belief like this that lasted for less than one month?
No, I've never had anything like this happen before. This is the first time I've ever dealt with something like this, and it's just been this past year.
Before this past year, have you usually had difficulty with close relationships or felt very socially अलग/withdrawn in the same way?

No, not at all. Before this past year, my relationships were fine. I had friends, I was close with my family... I definitely wasn't withdrawn or keeping to myself. Everything was pretty normal socially until all of this started happening.
